question: A newborn has a rapidly growing red skin lesion that appeared within weeks of birth and has shown partial regression by age 6. Which diagnosis best fits this presentation?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Hemangiomas

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma of skin lesion
options.rationale: Correct because infantile (strawberry) hemangiomas present within weeks of life, grow rapidly, and often involute over years. The lecture states: "Present within first few weeks of life (why it’s aka infantile hemangioma)" and "Complete involution in 50% of cases by age 5 years and 70% by age 7 years."

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma of deeper soft tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deeper, spongy, and tend not to regress; changing to a superficial, rapidly involuting lesion would make this correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma of oral mucosa lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas are rapidly growing red papules often after trauma and peak in young adults; if the lesion arose after trauma in a 20–30-year-old, this would be plausible.

options.text: Nevus flammeus port wine stain lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because nevus flammeus (port-wine stain) does not regress and often darkens over time; if the lesion were persistent without involution, this would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis from Bartonella infection
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis occurs in immunocompromised hosts and shows neutrophilic inflammation with organisms on silver stain; if the infant were immunocompromised with positive silver stain, this would be plausible.

question: Which histologic description best matches a lesion composed of closely packed, thin-walled, blood-filled capillaries lined by flattened endothelium in the dermis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Capillary hemangioma

options.text: Collection of closely packed thin walled capillaries
options.rationale: Correct because capillary hemangiomas are described as a collection of closely packed, thin-walled, blood-filled capillaries lined by flattened endothelium in the dermis. The lecture states: "Skin, dermis: Collection of closely packed, thin walled, blood-filled capillaries lined by flattened endothelium."

options.text: Cystically dilated cavernous blood filled vessels
options.rationale: Incorrect because that description fits cavernous hemangioma; if channels were large and cystic rather than capillary-sized, this option would be correct.

options.text: Proliferating capillaries with edema and inflammation
options.rationale: Incorrect because that pattern describes pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma); if the lesion had prominent inflammation and ulceration, this would be appropriate.

options.text: Dilated lymphatic channels within dermal layer
options.rationale: Incorrect because dilated lymphatic channels indicate lymphangioma; if the channels contained lymph rather than blood, this would be correct.

options.text: Anastomosing vascular channels with marked atypia
options.rationale: Incorrect because anastomosing channels with cellular atypia suggest angiosarcoma; if there were marked nuclear pleomorphism and invasion, this would be correct.

question: A lesion composed of larger, cystically dilated vascular channels that is deeper and tends not to regress most likely corresponds to which entity?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Cavernous hemangioma

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma of deeper soft tissue
options.rationale: Correct because cavernous hemangiomas have larger, dilated vascular channels, are more deeply located, and tend not to regress. The lecture notes: "Have larger more dilated vascular channels (spongy)" and "Tend to be more deeply located" and "Tend not to regress."

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma of skin lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are superficial and often involute; if the channels were small and superficial with involution, this would be correct.

options.text: Lymphangioma with dilated lymphatic channels
options.rationale: Incorrect because lymphangiomas involve lymphatic channels rather than blood-filled cavernous vessels; if the fluid were lymphatic and not blood-filled, this would be correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma with exuberant granulation tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas are capillary proliferations with inflammation and often ulcerate; if the lesion were a rapidly bleeding papule with inflammatory infiltrate, this would be correct.

options.text: Angiosarcoma with malignant endothelial proliferation
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma shows malignant endothelial cells and atypia; if there were marked cellular pleomorphism and invasion, this would be correct.

question: Which vascular proliferation is a reactive lesion seen in immunocompromised patients caused by Bartonella species and can mimic Kaposi sarcoma clinically?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Bacillary angiomatosis

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis from Bartonella infection
options.rationale: Correct because bacillary angiomatosis is an opportunistic infection with Bartonella spp. in immunocompromised individuals and can resemble Kaposi sarcoma. The lecture states: "Reactive vascular proliferation... Opportunistic infection with Bartonella spp. in immunocompromised individuals" and notes clinical resemblance to Kaposi sarcoma.

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma from HHV eight infection
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 and is a neoplasm rather than a reactive bacterial proliferation; if viral HHV-8 infection with spindle cell proliferation were present, this would be correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma following local trauma to skin
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granuloma is a lobular capillary hemangioma often following trauma and not an infectious proliferation; if there were a history of trauma and granulation tissue histology, this would be correct.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma congenital deep vascular malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangioma is a congenital vascular malformation with large dilated channels and not infection-related; if the lesion were congenital and noninflammatory, this would be correct.

options.text: Spider angioma from chronic liver disease
options.rationale: Incorrect because spider angiomas are acquired telangiectasias associated with hyperestrogenism and liver disease, not infectious vascular proliferations; if multiple spider angiomas and liver disease were present, this would be correct.

question: A 35-year-old man with HIV has multiple violaceous skin patches that progress to nodules. Which etiologic agent is most directly implicated in this vascular neoplasm?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Kaposi sarcoma

options.text: Human herpesvirus eight infection of endothelial cells
options.rationale: Correct because Kaposi sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV) infection and is common in immunosuppressed patients. The lecture states: "Low- to intermediate-grade vascular... neoplasm caused by human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) infection."

options.text: Bartonella henselae infection causing vascular proliferation
options.rationale: Incorrect because Bartonella causes bacillary angiomatosis, not Kaposi sarcoma; if silver stain showed bacilli and the patient were immunocompromised, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Polyvinyl chloride exposure causing hepatic angiosarcoma
options.rationale: Incorrect because polyvinyl chloride exposure is linked to hepatic angiosarcoma, not Kaposi sarcoma; if the patient had occupational PVC exposure and liver tumor, angiosarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Arsenic exposure leading to cutaneous vascular tumors
options.rationale: Incorrect because arsenic exposure is associated with hepatic angiosarcoma and other malignancies; if there were documented arsenic exposure and hepatic lesions, angiosarcoma would be plausible.

options.text: Mutation in VHL gene causing vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL mutations are associated with hemangioblastoma, not Kaposi sarcoma; if CNS hemangioblastomas and VHL features were present, VHL would be implicated.

question: Which vascular tumor is described as malignant endothelial proliferation that often arises in sun-exposed skin and is associated with exposures such as arsenic and polyvinyl chloride?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Angiosarcoma/hemangiosarcoma

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant tumor of endothelial cells
options.rationale: Correct because angiosarcoma is a malignant tumor of endothelial cells that can occur in skin, soft tissue, breast, and liver and is associated with carcinogens like arsenic and polyvinyl chloride. The lecture notes: "Malignant tumor of endothelial cells... Hepatic angiosarcomas are associated with carcinogen exposures" and lists arsenic and polyvinyl chloride.

options.text: Hemangioma benign overgrowth of blood vessel tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because hemangiomas are benign collections of blood vessels and often involute; if the lesion lacked atypia and invasion, hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma HHV eight associated vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma is HHV-8 associated and lower grade; if HHV-8 infection and spindle cell histology were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis reactive Bartonella vascular proliferation
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis is infectious and reactive in immunocompromised hosts; if silver stain showed bacilli, this would be the diagnosis.

options.text: Hemangioendothelioma intermediate grade vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because hemangioendothelioma is intermediate-grade and distinct from high-grade angiosarcoma; if histology showed intermediate features without marked pleomorphism, hemangioendothelioma would be considered.

question: A child presents with a multiloculated cystic mass in the neck consistent with a cavernous lymphatic malformation. Which syndrome is commonly associated with this finding?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Lymphangioma

options.text: Turner syndrome associated with cystic hygroma formation
options.rationale: Correct because cystic hygroma (a form of cavernous lymphangioma) commonly occurs in the neck and is associated with Turner syndrome. The lecture states: "Cystic hygroma is a form of cavernous lymphangioma... Common in Turner syndrome."

options.text: Tuberous sclerosis associated with cardiac rhabdomyomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because tuberous sclerosis is associated with cardiac rhabdomyomas, not cystic hygromas; if cardiac tumors and cortical tubers were present, TSC would be implicated.

options.text: von Hippel Lindau associated with CNS hemangioblastomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL is associated with hemangioblastomas of the CNS and retina; if CNS vascular tumors and VHL gene deletion were present, VHL would be correct.

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with mucosal telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHT causes telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations, not cystic hygromas; if recurrent epistaxis and mucosal telangiectasias were present, HHT would be likely.

options.text: Sturge Weber syndrome with facial port wine stain
options.rationale: Incorrect because Sturge-Weber features nevus flammeus and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if facial port-wine stain and seizures were present, Sturge-Weber would be correct.

question: Which lesion is a painful, small tumor usually located beneath fingernails and arises from modified smooth muscle cells of thermoregulatory arteriovenous structures?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Glomus tumor

options.text: Glomus tumor of glomus body under nail
options.rationale: Correct because glomus tumors arise from modified smooth muscle glomus cells in glomus bodies, are small, painful, and often occur under fingernails. The lecture states: "Benign tumor of modified smooth muscle cells (glomus cells)... Usually occur under fingernails" and notes pain.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma rapidly bleeding capillary papule lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas are capillary proliferations that bleed easily and often follow trauma; if the lesion were an ulcerated bleeding papule, this would be plausible.

options.text: Capillary hemangioma infantile superficial strawberry lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are infantile and typically superficial on head and neck; if the lesion were in an infant and involuting, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep spongy vascular malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deeper with large dilated channels and not characteristically painful under nails; if deep cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor of skin
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma is malignant with atypia and aggressive behavior; if biopsy showed marked pleomorphism and invasion, angiosarcoma would be considered.

question: Which congenital vascular birthmark does not regress and may darken or thicken over time, often called a port-wine stain?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Nevus flammeus

options.text: Nevus flammeus port wine stain congenital lesion
options.rationale: Correct because nevus flammeus (port-wine stain) does not regress and may darken or thicken over time. The lecture states: "Unlike some other birthmarks (e.g., hemangioma), nevus flammeus does not regress and may darken or thicken over time."

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma strawberry mark that involutes
options.rationale: Incorrect because infantile hemangiomas often involute over years; if the lesion showed progressive involution, infantile hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Cystic hygroma lymphatic malformation in neck region
options.rationale: Incorrect because cystic hygromas are lymphatic and often present as multiloculated neck masses; if the lesion were cystic and fluctuant in the neck, cystic hygroma would be correct.

options.text: Spider angioma acquired telangiectasia from liver disease
options.rationale: Incorrect because spider angiomas are acquired telangiectasias associated with hyperestrogenism and liver disease; if multiple spider angiomas and cirrhosis were present, this would be correct.

options.text: Glomus tumor painful subungual thermoregulatory lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because glomus tumors are painful subungual lesions; if severe localized nailbed pain were the main feature, glomus tumor would be likely.

question: A patient with facial port-wine stain over the trigeminal distribution, seizures, and leptomeningeal vascular malformations most likely has which diagnosis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Sturge-Weber syndrome

options.text: Sturge Weber syndrome with leptomeningeal angiomatosis
options.rationale: Correct because Sturge-Weber (encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis) features a facial nevus flammeus in the trigeminal distribution and leptomeningeal vascular malformations causing seizures. The lecture states: "Characterized by: Nevus flammeus (port-wine stain) of the face- distributed over the trigeminal nerve" and notes leptomeningeal vascular abnormalities and seizures.

options.text: Tuberous sclerosis complex with cortical tubers and rhabdomyomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because tuberous sclerosis presents with cortical tubers, seizures, and cardiac rhabdomyomas; if cardiac tumors and ash leaf spots were present, TSC would be correct.

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with mucosal telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHT causes mucocutaneous telangiectasias and bleeding, not leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if recurrent epistaxis and GI bleeding were present, HHT would be likely.

options.text: Neurofibromatosis type one with café au lait spots
options.rationale: Incorrect because NF1 features neurofibromas and café-au-lait spots rather than port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if multiple neurofibromas and Lisch nodules were present, NF1 would be correct.

options.text: Von Hippel Lindau disease with retinal hemangioblastomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL causes hemangioblastomas in CNS and retina and renal tumors, not facial port-wine stains; if retinal hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma were present, VHL would be considered.

question: A 5-year-old boy has conjunctival telangiectasias, progressive ataxia, immunodeficiency, and increased risk of leukemia. Which genetic defect best explains this constellation?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Ataxia telangiectasia

options.text: Mutation in ATM gene causing defective DNA repair
options.rationale: Correct because ataxia telangiectasia is due to ATM mutation, affecting double-strand DNA break response, causing ataxia, conjunctival telangiectasias, immunodeficiency, and increased malignancy risk. The lecture states: "Autosomal recessive genetic disorder (mutation in ATM)" and "ATM plays role in response to double-stranded DNA breaks and development of the nervous and immune systems."

options.text: Mutation in ENG gene causing vascular malformations
options.rationale: Incorrect because ENG mutations cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) with mucocutaneous telangiectasias and bleeding; if recurrent epistaxis and AV malformations were present, ENG mutation would be correct.

options.text: Deletion of VHL gene causing hemangioblastomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL deletion causes hemangioblastomas and VHL syndrome features; if CNS hemangioblastomas and renal tumors were present, VHL would be implicated.

options.text: TSC1 or TSC2 mutation causing hamartomatous tumors
options.rationale: Incorrect because TSC mutations cause tuberous sclerosis with rhabdomyomas and cortical tubers; if cardiac rhabdomyomas and ash leaf spots were present, TSC would be correct.

options.text: GNAQ activating mutation causing port wine stain
options.rationale: Incorrect because activating GNAQ mutations underlie Sturge-Weber syndrome with port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if facial port-wine stain and leptomeningeal calcifications were present, GNAQ mutation would be correct.

question: Which vascular lesion is most likely to present as a rapidly growing red papule on the oral mucosa of a pregnant woman that often regresses after delivery?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Pyogenic granuloma / Lobular Capillary Hemangioma

options.text: Pregnancy associated pyogenic granuloma of mucosa
options.rationale: Correct because pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma) can occur in pregnancy (granuloma gravidarum), presents as a rapidly growing red papule on skin or oral mucosa, and often regresses post-delivery. The lecture notes: "Pregnancy tumor (granuloma gravidarum)- a pyogenic granuloma that occurs in ~1% of pregnant women; often regresses post-delivery."

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma strawberry mark of infancy
options.rationale: Incorrect because infantile capillary hemangiomas present in infancy and involute over years; if the lesion appeared in a neonate, this would be correct.

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma HHV eight associated vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma is HHV-8 related and typically occurs in immunosuppressed adults; if HHV-8 infection and spindle cell histology were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis Bartonella infection in immunocompromised
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis occurs in immunocompromised hosts and shows organisms on silver stain; if the patient were immunocompromised with positive silver stain, this would be likely.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep cystic vascular malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deeper and do not typically present as rapidly bleeding mucosal papules in pregnancy; if deep cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be considered.

question: Which cardiac tumor is most common in adults, often arises in the atria, and can cause ball-valve obstruction leading to syncope or dyspnea?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Cardiac myxomas

options.text: Atrial myxoma pedunculated left atrial mass
options.rationale: Correct because myxomas are the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults, 90% are located in the atria (left more common), and can cause ball-valve obstruction. The lecture states: "Most common primary tumor of the heart in adults" and "90% are located in the atria; 4:1 left to right ratio" and notes ball-valve obstruction.

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma multiple infantile ventricular nodules
options.rationale: Incorrect because rhabdomyomas are most common in infants and children and often regress; if the patient were an infant with tuberous sclerosis, rhabdomyoma would be likely.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular surface tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small tumors on valve surfaces and less likely to cause large atrial obstruction; if a small valvular mass were seen, this would be considered.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma benign fatty intracardiac mass
options.rationale: Incorrect because cardiac lipomas are benign fatty tumors and less commonly cause ball-valve obstruction; if imaging showed a fatty mass, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic carcinoma involving pericardium and myocardium
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic tumors to the heart are more common than primary tumors but typically present with pericardial involvement; if there were known widespread malignancy, metastasis would be likely.

question: A pediatric patient is found to have multiple well-circumscribed white nodules in the myocardium composed of vacuolated cardiac myocytes called spider cells. Which diagnosis is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Rhabdomyomas

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma with vacuolated spider cells
options.rationale: Correct because cardiac rhabdomyomas are composed of large, vacuolated cardiac myocytes (spider cells), are the most common primary cardiac tumor in infants and children, and may be multiple. The lecture states: "Cardiac rhabdomyomas are well-circumscribed and composed of large, vacuolated (due to high glycogen content) cardiac myocytes" and mentions spider cells.

options.text: Atrial myxoma pedunculated left atrial mass lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because myxomas occur in adults and have abundant myxoid matrix rather than vacuolated myocytes; if the patient were an adult with an atrial pedunculated mass, myxoma would be likely.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma benign fatty intracardiac tumor mass
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are composed of adipose tissue, not vacuolated myocytes; if imaging showed fatty composition, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic neuroblastoma involving myocardium in child
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic tumors have different histology and are less likely to show spider cells; if there were a primary neuroblastoma with cardiac metastases, metastasis would be considered.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular papillary tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small valvular tumors composed of connective tissue and elastin, not vacuolated myocytes; if a small valvular lesion were present, fibroelastoma would be likely.

question: Which genetic syndrome is associated with multiple cardiac myxomas, pigmented skin lesions, and endocrine overactivity?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Carney complex

options.text: Carney complex autosomal dominant myxoma syndrome
options.rationale: Correct because Carney complex is an autosomal dominant syndrome associated with multiple cardiac and extracardiac myxomas, pigmented skin lesions, and endocrine overactivity. The lecture states: "Carney complex... Multiple cardiac and often extracardiac (e.g., skin) myxomas, pigmented skin lesions, and endocrine over-activity."

options.text: Tuberous sclerosis complex with rhabdomyomas and cortical tubers
options.rationale: Incorrect because TSC is associated with rhabdomyomas and cortical tubers, not multiple myxomas and endocrine overactivity; if cardiac rhabdomyomas and ash leaf spots were present, TSC would be correct.

options.text: Von Hippel Lindau with hemangioblastomas and renal tumors
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL features hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma, not multiple myxomas; if retinal hemangioblastomas and renal tumors were present, VHL would be likely.

options.text: Neurofibromatosis type one with neurofibromas and café au lait
options.rationale: Incorrect because NF1 causes neurofibromas and café-au-lait spots, not myxomas and endocrine overactivity; if multiple neurofibromas were present, NF1 would be correct.

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with mucosal telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHT causes telangiectasias and bleeding, not cardiac myxomas and endocrine tumors; if recurrent epistaxis and AV malformations were present, HHT would be likely.

question: Which vascular lesion is characterized microscopically by proliferating capillaries with edema and inflammatory infiltrate and often follows trauma?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Pyogenic granuloma / Lobular Capillary Hemangioma

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary hemangioma lesion
options.rationale: Correct because pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma) shows proliferating capillaries, edema, and inflammatory infiltrate and often develops after trauma. The lecture describes: "Microscopic: proliferating capillaries + edema + inflammatory infiltrate…similar to exuberant granulation tissue" and notes association with trauma.

options.text: Capillary hemangioma infantile superficial strawberry vascular lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are infantile lesions that involute over time and lack the prominent inflammatory granulation tissue pattern; if the lesion were an infantile superficial strawberry mark, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis Bartonella induced vascular proliferation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis shows neutrophilic inflammation and organisms on silver stain in immunocompromised hosts; if silver stain revealed bacilli, this would be likely.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep cystic blood filled malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas have large dilated channels and thrombosis, not the lobular capillary proliferation with inflammation; if deep cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Granulation tissue normal reparative vascular fibroblastic tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because granulation tissue is part of normal repair and not a discrete tumor; if the lesion were within a week of injury and part of healing, granulation tissue would be the explanation.

question: A 55-year-old man with chronic liver disease has multiple spider-like telangiectasias on the chest. Which mechanism best explains their development in this context?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Vascular ectasias (to include potential etiologies and associated disorders)

options.text: Hyperestrogenism from reduced hepatic steroid clearance
options.rationale: Correct because chronic liver disease reduces clearance of circulating steroids leading to hyperestrogenism, which contributes to spider angiomas. The lecture notes: "Causes include... Liver disease- reduced clearance of circulating steroids (estrogen)→ hyperestrogenism" and shows spider angiomas in cirrhosis.

options.text: Direct Bartonella infection causing vascular proliferation lesions
options.rationale: Incorrect because Bartonella causes bacillary angiomatosis in immunocompromised hosts, not spider angiomas from liver disease; if silver stain showed bacilli and the patient were immunocompromised, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Mutation in ENG gene causing mucocutaneous telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because ENG mutations cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with mucosal telangiectasias and bleeding, not spider angiomas from liver disease; if recurrent epistaxis and AV malformations were present, HHT would be correct.

options.text: Sun exposure induced telangiectasia of superficial dermis
options.rationale: Incorrect because sun exposure can cause telangiectasias but the mechanism in chronic liver disease is hormonal; if the lesions were limited to sun-exposed skin without liver disease, sun-induced telangiectasia would be plausible.

options.text: Autoimmune destruction of small dermal blood vessels
options.rationale: Incorrect because autoimmune vasculitis causes vessel inflammation and damage rather than dilated spider angiomas; if biopsy showed vasculitis with inflammatory infiltrate, autoimmune vasculitis would be considered.

question: Which lesion is best described as an overgrowth of tissue native to the site and is often used to characterize many hemangiomas?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Hemangiomas (hamartoma vs choristoma)

options.text: Hamartoma abnormal overgrowth of native tissue at site
options.rationale: Correct because a hamartoma is an abnormal overgrowth of tissue native to the site; many hemangiomas (strawberry marks) are considered vascular hamartomas. The lecture states: "Hamartoma- abnormal (overgrowth of) tissue in a normal/native site" and notes hemangiomas may be hamartomas.

options.text: Choristoma normal tissue in an abnormal non native site
options.rationale: Incorrect because a choristoma is normal tissue in an abnormal site; if normal tissue were found in a non-native location (e.g., hair-bearing skin in the cornea), choristoma would be correct.

options.text: Neoplasm clonal proliferative tumor with autonomous growth
options.rationale: Incorrect because neoplasms are clonal and autonomous; if molecular evidence of clonal proliferation were present, labeling as neoplasm would be appropriate.

options.text: Vascular ectasia dilation of preexisting blood vessels without neoplasia
options.rationale: Incorrect because vascular ectasias are dilations of existing vessels, not overgrowths of native tissue; if the lesion were simply dilated vessels without proliferation, ectasia would be correct.

options.text: Reactive proliferation due to infectious organism presence
options.rationale: Incorrect because reactive proliferations like bacillary angiomatosis are infection-driven; if organisms were identified and inflammation present, reactive proliferation would be likely.

question: A biopsy of a cutaneous tumor shows sheets of plump spindle cells forming slit-like vascular spaces and likely lymphatic endothelial origin. Which diagnosis is most consistent?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Kaposi sarcoma

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma spindle cell vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Correct because Kaposi sarcoma shows proliferating spindle cells (likely lymphatic endothelial cells) forming vascular spaces. The lecture describes: "Histologic appearance of nodular form, demonstrating sheets of plump, proliferating spindle cells (likely lymphatic endothelial cells)."

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with marked atypia
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma shows malignant endothelial cells with marked pleomorphism and atypia; if there were high-grade nuclear atypia and invasion, angiosarcoma would be favored.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis neutrophilic inflammation with bacilli present
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis shows acute neutrophilic inflammation and organisms on silver stain; if silver stain revealed bacilli, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary proliferation with edema
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granuloma shows lobular capillary proliferation with edema and inflammation rather than spindle cell sheets; if histology showed lobular capillaries and ulceration, pyogenic granuloma would be correct.

options.text: Hemangioma capillary proliferation of flattened endothelial cells
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are composed of flattened endothelial-lined capillaries, not spindle cell sheets; if the biopsy showed closely packed capillaries lined by flattened endothelium, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

question: Which hepatic exposure history would most strongly raise suspicion for a primary hepatic angiosarcoma on imaging?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Angiosarcoma (hepatic associations)

options.text: Occupational polyvinyl chloride exposure with hepatic lesions
options.rationale: Correct because hepatic angiosarcomas are associated with exposures such as polyvinyl chloride and arsenic. The lecture states: "Hepatic angiosarcomas are associated with carcinogen exposures" and lists polyvinyl chloride and arsenic.

options.text: Chronic hepatitis C infection causing regenerative nodules
options.rationale: Incorrect because chronic hepatitis C leads to cirrhosis and regenerative nodules rather than angiosarcoma; if imaging showed cirrhotic nodularity and history of hepatitis C, cirrhosis would be more likely.

options.text: Alcoholic liver disease with multiple spider angiomas present
options.rationale: Incorrect because alcoholic liver disease causes cirrhosis and spider angiomas but is not a specific risk factor for hepatic angiosarcoma; if cirrhosis signs predominated, cirrhosis would be the diagnosis.

options.text: HHV eight infection causing vascular hepatic tumors
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma, not hepatic angiosarcoma; if HHV-8 positive spindle cell lesions were found, Kaposi sarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Bartonella infection in immunocompromised patient with lesions
options.rationale: Incorrect because Bartonella causes bacillary angiomatosis, typically cutaneous or visceral in immunocompromised hosts, not hepatic angiosarcoma; if silver stain showed bacilli, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

question: A 34-year-old HIV-positive woman has multiple red nodules; biopsy shows neutrophilic inflammation and vascular proliferation with rod-shaped curved bacteria on silver stain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Bacillary angiomatosis

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis due to Bartonella species infection
options.rationale: Correct because bacillary angiomatosis presents in immunocompromised patients with vascular proliferation and neutrophilic inflammation; silver stain demonstrates clusters of bacilli. The lecture notes: "Bacillary angiomatosis... Opportunistic infection with Bartonella spp. in immunocompromised individuals" and shows silver stain findings.

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma HHV eight associated spindle cell neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma shows spindle cell proliferation and is HHV-8 associated; if biopsy showed spindle cells without organisms, Kaposi sarcoma would be likely.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary hemangioma after trauma
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas have lobular capillary proliferation with edema and inflammation but lack organisms on silver stain; if there were a history of trauma and no organisms, pyogenic granuloma would be plausible.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep cystic blood filled malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are congenital vascular malformations with large dilated channels and thrombosis, not neutrophilic inflammation with organisms; if deep cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with cellular atypia
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma shows malignant endothelial atypia and anastomosing channels, not neutrophilic inflammation with bacteria; if biopsy showed marked pleomorphism, angiosarcoma would be considered.

question: Which cardiac tumor in infants is frequently associated with tuberous sclerosis complex and may regress spontaneously?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Rhabdomyomas and association with TSC

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma associated with tuberous sclerosis complex
options.rationale: Correct because cardiac rhabdomyomas are the most common primary cardiac tumor in infants and about 50% are associated with tuberous sclerosis; they may regress spontaneously. The lecture states: "~50% due to sporadic mutations and ~50% are associated with Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC)" and notes possible regression.

options.text: Atrial myxoma most common primary adult cardiac tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because atrial myxomas are most common in adults, not infants; if the patient were an adult with an atrial mass, myxoma would be likely.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma benign fatty intracardiac tumor in adults
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are benign fatty tumors and not specifically associated with TSC or infantile regression; if imaging showed fatty composition, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular tumor in adults
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small valvular tumors typically in adults; if a small valvular mass were present, fibroelastoma would be considered.

options.text: Metastatic neuroblastoma to heart from pediatric primary
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic disease to the heart is more common than primary tumors but would have histology matching the primary tumor; if a known neuroblastoma with cardiac metastases existed, metastasis would be likely.

question: Which lesion is best classified as a dilation of preexisting blood vessels rather than a neoplasm and can be congenital or acquired?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Vascular ectasias / Telangiectasias

options.text: Vascular ectasia telangiectasia dilation of vessels
options.rationale: Correct because vascular ectasias/telangiectasias are dilations of preexisting blood vessels and are not neoplasms; they can be congenital or acquired. The lecture states: "Vascular ectasias / Telangiectasias: Dilation of preexisting blood vessels. Not neoplasms."

options.text: Hemangioma benign neoplasm of endothelial cells
options.rationale: Incorrect because hemangiomas are benign proliferations (or hamartomas) of endothelial cells rather than simple dilations; if there were a proliferative lesion of vessels, hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Lymphangioma benign lymphatic channel proliferation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because lymphangiomas are benign lymphatic proliferations, not dilations of blood vessels; if channels contained lymph and not blood, lymphangioma would be correct.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with invasion
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma is malignant and invasive, not a simple dilation; if biopsy showed malignant endothelial cells, angiosarcoma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis infectious vascular proliferation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis is an infectious reactive proliferation in immunocompromised hosts, not a nonproliferative dilation; if organisms were present, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

question: Which tumor is most likely to cause embolic phenomena or obstructive cardiac symptoms due to a pedunculated mass arising near the fossa ovalis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Myxomas (clinical effects)

options.text: Left atrial myxoma pedunculated mass from fossa ovalis
options.rationale: Correct because left atrial myxomas commonly arise near the fossa ovalis, are pedunculated, and can cause ball-valve obstruction or embolic events. The lecture describes a left atrial myxoma arising from the fossa ovalis and notes ball-valve obstruction and valve damage causing symptoms.

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma multiple intramyocardial nodules in infants
options.rationale: Incorrect because rhabdomyomas are intramyocardial and seen in infants, less likely to be pedunculated atrial masses; if multiple intramyocardial nodules in an infant were present, rhabdomyoma would be likely.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular papillary tumor causing emboli
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small valvular tumors that can embolize but are typically valvular rather than large pedunculated atrial masses; if a small valvular lesion were seen, fibroelastoma would be considered.

options.text: Metastatic melanoma involving endocardium and causing obstruction
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastases can involve the heart and cause obstruction but are usually in the setting of widespread malignancy; if there were known metastatic disease, metastasis would be likely.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma large fatty intracavitary mass causing symptoms
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are fatty and less commonly pedunculated from the fossa ovalis; if imaging showed a fatty composition mass, lipoma would be correct.

question: Which vascular tumor is considered intermediate-grade and sits between benign hemangiomas and malignant angiosarcomas in behavior?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Kaposi sarcoma and hemangioendothelioma (intermediate-grade neoplasms)

options.text: Hemangioendothelioma intermediate grade vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Correct because hemangioendothelioma is classified as an intermediate-grade vascular neoplasm between benign hemangiomas and malignant angiosarcomas. The lecture lists "INTERMEDIATE-GRADE NEOPLASMS: Kaposi sarcoma Hemangioendothelioma."

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma low to intermediate grade vascular tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because while Kaposi sarcoma is low- to intermediate-grade, the question asked for the intermediate-grade entity specifically named hemangioendothelioma; if the focus were Kaposi sarcoma specifically, that option would be appropriate.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma benign deep vascular malformation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are benign vascular malformations and not intermediate-grade neoplasms; if the lesion were benign and deep without aggressive features, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Angiosarcoma high grade malignant endothelial tumor lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma is malignant and high-grade, not intermediate; if biopsy showed marked atypia and invasion, angiosarcoma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis reactive infectious vascular proliferation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis is reactive and infectious, not an intermediate-grade neoplasm; if organisms were identified, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

question: A patient with multiple mucocutaneous telangiectasias, recurrent epistaxis, and family history of similar bleeding likely has which inherited disorder?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler Weber Rendu)

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia autosomal dominant disorder
options.rationale: Correct because HHT (Osler-Weber-Rendu) is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by widespread telangiectasias and bleeding such as epistaxis. The lecture states: "Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT)... Telangiectasias widely distributed... Dilated vessels may rupture and cause bleeding (e.g., epistaxis)."

options.text: Ataxia telangiectasia autosomal recessive with conjunctival telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because ataxia telangiectasia includes neurologic deficits and immunodeficiency in early childhood, not isolated mucocutaneous telangiectasias with adult onset; if ataxia and immunodeficiency were present in a child, AT would be considered.

options.text: Sturge Weber syndrome sporadic port wine stain and seizures
options.rationale: Incorrect because Sturge-Weber features facial port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis with seizures, not widespread mucosal telangiectasias and bleeding; if facial port-wine stain and seizures were present, Sturge-Weber would be likely.

options.text: Cushing syndrome hypercortisolism causing acquired telangiectasias
options.rationale: Incorrect because Cushing syndrome can cause acquired telangiectasias but not the familial pattern with recurrent epistaxis; if hypercortisolism signs were present, Cushing syndrome would be plausible.

options.text: Scleroderma CREST variant with telangiectasias and calcinosis
options.rationale: Incorrect because CREST (limited scleroderma) includes telangiectasias but usually with other systemic features and not a strong familial bleeding history; if sclerodactyly and esophageal dysmotility were present, CREST would be considered.

question: Which lesion is described grossly as a rapidly growing red papule often with an epithelial collarette at the base and bleeds easily?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Pyogenic granuloma

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma rapidly growing bleeding red papule
options.rationale: Correct because pyogenic granulomas present grossly as rapidly growing red papules often with an epithelial collarette and bleed easily. The lecture describes: "Gross: rapidly growing red papule on skin or oral mucosa; often with epithelial collarette at base; bleeds easily & often ulcerated."

options.text: Capillary hemangioma infantile strawberry superficial vascular lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are infantile and may involute over years rather than presenting as an ulcerated bleeding papule with collarette; if the lesion were an infantile strawberry mark, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis nodular lesions with neutrophilic inflammation
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis lesions may resemble pyogenic granuloma but are infectious with neutrophilic inflammation and organisms on silver stain; if silver stain were positive for bacilli, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma violaceous macules progressing to nodules
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma typically begins as violaceous macules or patches progressing to plaques and nodules, not necessarily with an epithelial collarette; if HHV-8 infection and spindle cell histology were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep spongy blood filled mass
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deeper and spongy with large dilated channels rather than superficial rapidly bleeding papules; if deep cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

question: Which primary cardiac tumor is most likely to present in adults and is thought to arise from primitive multipotent mesenchymal cells?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Myxoma origin and demographics

options.text: Cardiac myxoma arising from multipotent mesenchymal cells
options.rationale: Correct because myxomas are the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults and are thought to arise from primitive multipotent mesenchymal cells. The lecture states: "Thought to arise from primitive multipotent mesenchymal cells" and "Most common primary tumor of the heart in adults."

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma arising from cardiac myocytes in infants
options.rationale: Incorrect because rhabdomyomas arise from cardiac myocytes and are most common in infants and children; if the patient were an infant, rhabdomyoma would be likely.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma arising from valvular endocardium
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas arise from valvular endocardium and are small papillary tumors, not multipotent mesenchymal cell-derived atrial myxomas; if a small valvular lesion were present, fibroelastoma would be considered.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma benign fatty tumor of myocardium
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are benign fatty tumors and not derived from multipotent mesenchymal cells in the same way as myxomas; if imaging showed fatty composition, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic carcinoma to heart from distant primary tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic tumors to the heart are more common than primary tumors but are secondary; if there were known widespread malignancy, metastasis would be likely.

question: Which lesion is characterized microscopically by abundant amorphous extracellular matrix rich in glycosaminoglycans with scattered myxoma cells and abnormal vessel-like formations?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Myxoma histology

options.text: Cardiac myxoma with abundant myxoid extracellular matrix
options.rationale: Correct because myxomas have abundant amorphous extracellular matrix (GAGs) with scattered myxoma cells and abnormal vessel-like formations. The lecture includes an image description: "Microscopic appearance, with abundant amorphous extracellular matrix (GAGs) in which there are scattered collections of myxoma cells..."

options.text: Rhabdomyoma composed of vacuolated cardiac myocytes spider cells
options.rationale: Incorrect because rhabdomyomas are composed of vacuolated cardiac myocytes (spider cells) rather than abundant myxoid matrix; if vacuolated myocytes were present, rhabdomyoma would be correct.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma with papillary fronds on valve surface
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas have papillary fronds composed of connective tissue and elastin on valve surfaces, not myxoid GAG-rich matrix; if a valvular papillary lesion were seen, fibroelastoma would be likely.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma composed of mature adipose tissue nodules
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are composed of mature adipose tissue, not myxoid extracellular matrix; if histology showed adipocytes, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic mucinous carcinoma with extracellular mucin pools
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic mucinous carcinoma can show extracellular mucin but would have epithelial malignant cells and clinical history of carcinoma; if epithelial malignant cells and mucin were present, metastasis would be considered.

question: Which vascular tumor is most likely to present in older adults on sun-exposed skin and has a poor prognosis with rare five-year survival?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Angiosarcoma clinical features and prognosis

options.text: Cutaneous angiosarcoma aggressive malignant endothelial tumor
options.rationale: Correct because angiosarcoma often occurs in older adults on sun-exposed skin, is aggressive, locally invasive, metastasizes, and five-year survival is rare. The lecture states: "Older adults... most often occur in the skin (sun exposed areas)... AGGRESSIVE- locally invasive and will metastasize; survival greater than 5 years is rare."

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma low intermediate grade HHV eight tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma is low- to intermediate-grade and associated with HHV-8, not typically described as having rare five-year survival in older adults on sun-exposed skin; if HHV-8 infection and spindle cell histology were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma benign deep vascular malformation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are benign and not associated with poor prognosis; if the lesion were deep and noninvasive, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis infectious vascular proliferation in immunocompromised
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis is infectious and treatable, not typically fatal with rare five-year survival; if organisms were identified, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Hemangioendothelioma intermediate grade vascular tumor of soft tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because hemangioendothelioma is intermediate-grade and less aggressive than angiosarcoma; if histology showed intermediate features without marked pleomorphism, hemangioendothelioma would be considered.

question: A patient presents with a port-wine stain on the face and later develops focal seizures and ipsilateral hemiparesis. Imaging shows leptomeningeal vascular malformations with cortical calcifications. What is the most likely diagnosis?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Sturge-Weber syndrome (clinical vignette)

options.text: Sturge Weber syndrome encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis diagnosis
options.rationale: Correct because Sturge-Weber syndrome features facial port-wine stain in trigeminal distribution, leptomeningeal vascular malformations causing seizures, cortical calcifications, and neurologic deficits. The lecture states: "Characterized by: Nevus flammeus (port-wine stain) of the face- distributed over the trigeminal nerve" and notes leptomeningeal vascular abnormalities and seizures.

options.text: Tuberous sclerosis complex with cortical tubers and seizures
options.rationale: Incorrect because TSC causes cortical tubers and seizures but is associated with ash leaf spots and cardiac rhabdomyomas rather than port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if cardiac rhabdomyomas and ash leaf spots were present, TSC would be likely.

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with cerebral AV malformations
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHT causes mucocutaneous telangiectasias and AV malformations but not facial port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if recurrent epistaxis and mucosal telangiectasias were present, HHT would be considered.

options.text: Metastatic melanoma with leptomeningeal spread and seizures
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastatic melanoma can cause leptomeningeal disease but would have a history of melanoma and different skin findings; if there were known melanoma with leptomeningeal metastases, metastasis would be likely.

options.text: Neurofibromatosis type two with meningiomas and schwannomas
options.rationale: Incorrect because NF2 features bilateral vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas rather than port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomatosis; if bilateral schwannomas were present, NF2 would be correct.

question: Which vascular tumor of the central nervous system is composed of endothelial cells, pericytes, and stromal cells and is associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease in some cases?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Hemangioblastoma

options.text: Hemangioblastoma CNS vascular tumor associated with VHL
options.rationale: Correct because hemangioblastomas are benign CNS vascular tumors composed of endothelial cells, pericytes, and stromal cells and occur sporadically or as part of von Hippel-Lindau disease. The lecture states: "Benign vascular tumor of the central nervous system... Composed of endothelial cells, pericytes, and stromal cells" and notes association with VHL.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor of soft tissue and liver
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma is malignant and occurs in skin, soft tissue, breast, and liver, not typically as a benign CNS hemangioblastoma; if biopsy showed malignant endothelial atypia, angiosarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Capillary hemangioma superficial skin lesion in infants
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are superficial infantile skin lesions, not CNS tumors associated with VHL; if the lesion were a superficial infantile mark, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma to CNS in VHL patient
options.rationale: Incorrect because VHL patients can have renal cell carcinoma metastases, but hemangioblastomas are primary CNS vascular tumors; if imaging showed metastatic carcinoma with epithelial markers, metastasis would be likely.

options.text: Lymphangioma cystic hygroma of neck and axilla
options.rationale: Incorrect because lymphangiomas are lymphatic malformations of neck/axilla, not CNS vascular tumors; if a neck cystic mass were present, lymphangioma would be correct.

question: Which lesion is most likely when a skin biopsy shows anastomosing vascular channels lined by plump endothelial cells with marked cellular and nuclear polymorphism?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Angiosarcoma histology

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with atypia
options.rationale: Correct because angiosarcoma shows anastomosing vascular structures lined by plump endothelial cells with marked cellular and nuclear polymorphism. The lecture provides an image description: "Skin biopsy showing anastomosing vascular structures in the dermis lined by plump endothelial cells with marked cellular and nuclear polymorphism."

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma spindle cell vascular proliferation without marked atypia
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma shows spindle cell proliferation but typically lacks the marked pleomorphism seen in angiosarcoma; if spindle cells without high-grade atypia and HHV-8 positivity were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be likely.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis neutrophilic inflammation with bacilli on silver stain
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis shows neutrophilic inflammation and organisms on silver stain rather than malignant endothelial atypia; if silver stain revealed bacilli, bacillary angiomatosis would be correct.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma large dilated vascular channels with thrombosis
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas have large dilated channels and thrombosis without malignant atypia; if large cystic channels and thrombosis were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Hemangioendothelioma intermediate vascular tumor with less atypia
options.rationale: Incorrect because hemangioendotheliomas are intermediate-grade and show less marked atypia than angiosarcoma; if histology showed intermediate features without marked pleomorphism, hemangioendothelioma would be considered.

question: Which lesion is most likely when a newborn has a faint red spot behind the ear noted at one week of age that enlarges and brightens over months?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Capillary hemangioma (infantile presentation)

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma presenting as strawberry mark
options.rationale: Correct because infantile capillary hemangiomas present within the first few weeks of life, grow rapidly over months, and are commonly located on the head and neck. The lecture notes: "Present within first few weeks of life... Grow rapidly over several months" and that most common location is head & neck.

options.text: Nevus flammeus congenital port wine stain that persists
options.rationale: Incorrect because nevus flammeus is present at birth and does not typically show rapid postnatal growth or brightening in the same way; if the lesion were flat and persistent without growth, nevus flammeus would be likely.

options.text: Cystic hygroma lymphatic malformation in neck region
options.rationale: Incorrect because cystic hygromas are cystic lymphatic masses often in the neck and may be present at birth but are not superficial red spots; if a multiloculated cystic neck mass were present, cystic hygroma would be correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma trauma related rapidly bleeding papule
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas often follow trauma and peak in young adults, not neonates; if the lesion arose after trauma and bled easily, pyogenic granuloma would be plausible.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis infectious nodules in immunocompromised infant
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis occurs in immunocompromised hosts and shows organisms on silver stain; if the infant were immunocompromised with positive silver stain, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

question: Which cardiac tumor is most likely to be multiple, discovered in the first year of life, and associated with tuberous sclerosis in about half of cases?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Rhabdomyoma demographics and associations

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma multiple infantile tumors linked to TSC
options.rationale: Correct because cardiac rhabdomyomas are often multiple, discovered in infancy, and about 50% are associated with tuberous sclerosis complex. The lecture states: "Most common primary tumor of the heart in infants and children... May be multiple... ~50% due to sporadic mutations and ~50% are associated with Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC)."

options.text: Atrial myxoma solitary adult atrial pedunculated tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because atrial myxomas occur in adults and are usually solitary atrial masses; if the patient were an adult with a solitary atrial mass, myxoma would be likely.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma solitary fatty intracardiac mass in adults
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are fatty tumors typically in adults and not associated with TSC; if imaging showed fatty composition, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular tumor often incidental
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small valvular tumors and not typically multiple infantile masses associated with TSC; if a small valvular lesion were seen, fibroelastoma would be considered.

options.text: Metastatic neuroblastoma to heart from pediatric primary tumor
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastases to the heart would reflect a primary tumor elsewhere and have different histology; if there were known neuroblastoma with cardiac metastases, metastasis would be likely.

question: Which lesion is most likely when a skin birthmark on the nape of the neck (stork bite) fades over time rather than persisting or darkening?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Nevus flammeus variants and natural history

options.text: Midline nevus flammeus stork bite that often fades
options.rationale: Correct because certain nevus flammeus variants like the midline nuchal 'stork bite' often fade over time, unlike port-wine stains which persist and may darken. The lecture lists variants including "Nevus flammeus nuchae Stork bite Midline nevus flammeus Angel kiss" and notes differing natural histories.

options.text: Port wine stain nevus flammeus that does not regress
options.rationale: Incorrect because classic port-wine stains typically do not regress and may darken; if the lesion persisted and darkened, port-wine stain would be correct.

options.text: Infantile capillary hemangioma strawberry mark that involutes
options.rationale: Incorrect because infantile hemangiomas often involute over years but present as raised strawberry lesions rather than flat stork bites; if the lesion were raised and involuting, capillary hemangioma would be likely.

options.text: Cystic hygroma lymphatic malformation in posterior neck region
options.rationale: Incorrect because cystic hygromas are cystic lymphatic masses and do not present as superficial fading birthmarks; if a multiloculated cystic mass were present, cystic hygroma would be correct.

options.text: Congenital nevus pigmented lesion with hair growth present
options.rationale: Incorrect because congenital nevi are pigmented and may have hair, not the vascular blanching stork bite; if a pigmented hairy lesion were present, congenital nevus would be considered.

question: Which vascular lesion is most likely to thrombose within its dilated channels and be vulnerable to traumatic bleeding?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Cavernous hemangioma complications

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma with thrombosis and bleeding risk
options.rationale: Correct because cavernous hemangiomas have cystically dilated vascular channels where thrombosis is common and they are vulnerable to traumatic damage and bleeding. The lecture states: "Collection of closely packed, cystically-dilated/cavernous, blood-filled vessels lined by flattened endothelium. Thrombosis is common."

options.text: Capillary hemangioma superficial lesion that often involutes
options.rationale: Incorrect because capillary hemangiomas are superficial and often involute rather than showing frequent thrombosis in large channels; if the lesion were superficial and involuting, capillary hemangioma would be correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma ulcerated bleeding papule after trauma
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas bleed easily but are lobular capillary proliferations with inflammation rather than cavernous channels prone to thrombosis; if the lesion were an ulcerated bleeding papule, pyogenic granuloma would be likely.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant tumor with hemorrhage and invasion
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcomas can hemorrhage but are malignant with atypia and invasion, not simply cavernous dilated channels with thrombosis; if biopsy showed malignant endothelial cells, angiosarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Vascular ectasia dilated preexisting vessels without thrombosis
options.rationale: Incorrect because vascular ectasias are dilations of existing vessels and typically lack the cavernous channel thrombosis seen in cavernous hemangiomas; if the lesion were simple dilation without thrombosis, ectasia would be correct.

question: Which lesion is most likely when a skin biopsy from an AIDS patient shows spindle cell proliferation with HHV-8 positivity?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Kaposi sarcoma (AIDS-associated)

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma HHV eight associated spindle cell tumor
options.rationale: Correct because AIDS-associated Kaposi sarcoma presents with spindle cell proliferation and is caused by HHV-8 infection. The lecture states: "Low- to intermediate-grade vascular... neoplasm caused by human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) infection" and notes it is most common in AIDS patients.

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis Bartonella infection with neutrophilic infiltrate
options.rationale: Incorrect because bacillary angiomatosis shows neutrophilic inflammation and organisms on silver stain rather than HHV-8 positivity; if silver stain showed bacilli, bacillary angiomatosis would be likely.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with marked pleomorphism
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma is malignant with marked pleomorphism and not specifically HHV-8 positive; if biopsy showed high-grade atypia, angiosarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary proliferation after trauma
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas are lobular capillary proliferations often after trauma and lack HHV-8 positivity; if there were trauma history and lobular capillaries, pyogenic granuloma would be plausible.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep dilated vascular malformation lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deep dilated channels without HHV-8 association; if large cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

question: Which vascular lesion is most likely to be mistaken clinically for Kaposi sarcoma but is distinguished histologically by acute neutrophilic inflammation and silver stain–positive bacilli?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Bacillary angiomatosis vs Kaposi sarcoma

options.text: Bacillary angiomatosis infectious lesion with silver positive bacilli
options.rationale: Correct because bacillary angiomatosis can resemble Kaposi sarcoma clinically but shows acute neutrophilic inflammation and clusters of bacilli on Warthin-Starry silver stain. The lecture notes: "Bacillary angiomatosis... A, Photograph... B, Histologic appearance with acute neutrophilic inflammation and vascular (capillary) proliferation. (Inset) Demonstration... of clusters of tangled bacilli (black)."

options.text: Kaposi sarcoma HHV eight spindle cell vascular neoplasm
options.rationale: Incorrect because Kaposi sarcoma is HHV-8 associated and shows spindle cell proliferation without silver stain bacilli; if HHV-8 positivity and spindle cells were present, Kaposi sarcoma would be correct.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary hemangioma with granulation tissue
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas have lobular capillary proliferation and inflammation but lack organisms on silver stain; if there were trauma history and no organisms, pyogenic granuloma would be likely.

options.text: Angiosarcoma malignant endothelial tumor with anastomosing channels
options.rationale: Incorrect because angiosarcoma shows malignant endothelial atypia and anastomosing channels, not neutrophilic inflammation with bacilli; if biopsy showed marked pleomorphism, angiosarcoma would be considered.

options.text: Cavernous hemangioma deep spongy blood filled vascular malformation
options.rationale: Incorrect because cavernous hemangiomas are deep dilated channels and not infectious proliferations with bacilli; if large cystic channels were present, cavernous hemangioma would be correct.

question: Which lesion is most likely when a skin finding consists of a central dilated arteriole with radiating capillaries resembling spider legs and is associated with pregnancy or liver disease?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Spider angioma (acquired telangiectasia)

options.text: Spider angioma central arteriole with radiating capillaries
options.rationale: Correct because spider angiomas have a central dilated arteriole with radiating capillaries and are associated with pregnancy and liver disease. The lecture describes: "Spider angioma- central dilated arteriole from which numerous capillaries and venules radiate" and lists pregnancy and liver disease as causes.

options.text: Spider vein superficial dilated capillary network without central arteriole
options.rationale: Incorrect because spider veins are dilated capillaries resembling spider legs but lack the central arteriole characteristic of spider angiomas; if only superficial dilated capillaries were present without a central arteriole, spider vein would be correct.

options.text: Nevus flammeus congenital port wine stain persistent lesion
options.rationale: Incorrect because nevus flammeus is a congenital port-wine stain that persists and may thicken, not a central arteriole with radiating capillaries; if a persistent flat port-wine stain were present, nevus flammeus would be likely.

options.text: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia mucocutaneous telangiectasias and bleeding
options.rationale: Incorrect because HHT causes widespread mucocutaneous telangiectasias and bleeding, not isolated spider angiomas associated with pregnancy or liver disease; if recurrent epistaxis and family history were present, HHT would be considered.

options.text: Pyogenic granuloma lobular capillary proliferation often ulcerated
options.rationale: Incorrect because pyogenic granulomas are lobular capillary proliferations that ulcerate and bleed, not central arteriole lesions; if a rapidly growing ulcerated papule were present, pyogenic granuloma would be likely.

question: Which cardiac tumor is most likely to regress spontaneously and is often discovered because it obstructs blood flow in infancy?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify: Rhabdomyoma clinical course and presentation

options.text: Cardiac rhabdomyoma infant tumor that may regress spontaneously
options.rationale: Correct because cardiac rhabdomyomas are common in infants, may cause obstruction leading to early discovery, and can regress spontaneously. The lecture states: "Most common primary tumor of the heart in infants and children... Usually discovered in the first year of life due to obstruction... May regress spontaneously."

options.text: Atrial myxoma adult tumor causing ball valve obstruction
options.rationale: Incorrect because atrial myxomas occur in adults and cause ball-valve obstruction but are not known to regress spontaneously; if the patient were an adult with an atrial pedunculated mass, myxoma would be likely.

options.text: Papillary fibroelastoma small valvular tumor causing embolic events
options.rationale: Incorrect because papillary fibroelastomas are small valvular tumors that can embolize but are not infantile regressing tumors; if a small valvular lesion were present, fibroelastoma would be considered.

options.text: Cardiac lipoma benign fatty mass rarely regressing spontaneously
options.rationale: Incorrect because lipomas are benign fatty tumors that do not typically regress spontaneously in infancy; if imaging showed fatty composition, lipoma would be correct.

options.text: Metastatic tumor to heart from pediatric malignancy
options.rationale: Incorrect because metastases reflect a primary malignancy elsewhere and are unlikely to regress spontaneously; if there were known metastatic disease, metastasis would be likely.
